title: Kachin Jinghpaw–English Dictionary
author: Adapted from Rawang.org
subject: Language & Literature
summary: 12,093 entries, searchable English to Jinghpaw and Jinghpaw to English.
keywords: dictionary, vocabulary, Jinghpaw, English
permission: Original vocabulary and definitions: Rawang.org. Permission requested.

title: A Grammar of the Kachin Language
author: Ola Hanson
subject: Language & Literature
summary: An early grammar of the Jinghpaw (Kachin) language, written in English for learners. Hanson also created the Latin-based Jinghpaw writing system, which makes this a key historical source.
keywords: grammar, Jinghpaw, Ola Hanson, Kachin language, missionary
source: Internet Archive (digitized from the University of Michigan library)
permission: Public domain (listed as not in copyright)

title: Rawt Malan Labau
author: Du Up Daju Zau Bug Htan (compiled from the writings of Lamung Tu Jai)
subject: History
summary: A Jinghpaw-language history of the Kachin revolution, covering resistance to British colonial rule from 1885, earlier conflicts with Burmese kings, the goals of the Wunpawng nation, and the founding of the KIC and KIO.
keywords: Rawt Malan, revolution, KIO, KIC, Wunpawng history, Lamung Tu Jai

title: KachinLingo
author: KachinLingo Team
subject: Apps & Learning Sites
summary: An online platform for learning Kachin (Jinghpaw), with daily lessons, vocabulary practice by category, games, a dictionary, an alphabet guide and short stories.
keywords: learn Jinghpaw, lessons, vocabulary, alphabet, language learning

title: Gămung
author: Nbwi Sut Aung (developer)
subject: Apps & Learning Sites
summary: A free community app with posts and polls, public and private groups, a local marketplace (Gămung Mart), job listings (Gămung Jobs) and messaging. It's available on the web, iOS and Android.
keywords: community, app, marketplace, jobs, messaging

title: Kachin Alliance
author: Kachin Alliance
subject: Organisations
summary: An advocacy organization working for peace, justice and freedom for the Kachin people. Its site publishes press releases, statements and the RECAP Newsletter, and raises support for displaced people, refugees and emergency relief.
keywords: advocacy, human rights, IDPs, refugees, press releases, newsletter

title: Kachin Folktales Told in Jinghpaw
author: Keita Kurabe and team (Gumtung Lu Awng, Sumdu Ja Seng Roi, Hpauhkum Htu Bu, Labang Tu La, Gumtung Htu Nan, Lashi Seng Nan)
subject: Language & Literature
summary: A collection of 2,491 recorded Kachin folktales and narratives in Jinghpaw, gathered through community fieldwork in northern Myanmar. Most stories include Jinghpaw transcriptions, and many have English translations.
keywords: folktales, maumwi, oral tradition, stories, audio, Kachin migration, PARADISEC
source: PARADISEC (Pacific and Regional Archive for Digital Sources in Endangered Cultures)

title: Jinghpaw Hanson Version Bible (JHVT3)
author: Bible Society of Myanmar (publisher)
subject: Religion
summary: The complete Bible in Jinghpaw, Old and New Testaments, in the Hanson version. It can be read free online at Bible.com or in the YouVersion Bible App, and audio is available. Printed copies are available from the Bible Society of Myanmar.
keywords: Bible, Chyum Laika, Hanson, scripture, Jinghpaw Bible, YouVersion

title: Kachin American Baptist Association (KABA)
author: Kachin American Baptist Association
subject: Organisations
summary: An association of Kachin Baptist churches in the United States, serving Kachin emigrants from Myanmar. It promotes fellowship, service and cooperation among member churches, with ministries in evangelism, culture and literature, media, Christian education, youth (KABA Youth), and men's and women's groups. It also partners on theological programs and advocates for religious freedom in Burma.
keywords: KABA, Kachin Baptist, churches, diaspora, United States, KABA Youth, religious freedom

title: Legal Aid Network (LAN)
author: Legal Aid Network
subject: Organisations
summary: An independent organization promoting the rule of law and legal literacy in Burma's ethnic communities. It supports activists, civil society groups and lawyers working on human rights, runs the Federal Law Academy, and publishes reports, statements and diplomatic briefings on Burma.
keywords: legal aid, rule of law, human rights, Burma, federalism, reports, Federal Law Academy

title: Federal Law Academy
author: Federal Law Academy, Mai Ja Yang (listed on the Legal Aid Network website)
subject: Schools & Education
summary: A legal education institution founded in 2014 in Mai Ja Yang, Kachin State. It trains young people and civil society leaders in federalism, human rights, the rule of law and ethnic self-determination, and offers a two-year Diploma in Law. In January 2025, it announced a draft federal constitution.
keywords: Federal Law Academy, Mai Ja Yang, law school, federalism, human rights, Diploma in Law, Kachin State

title: Shachyen Shaga Hkrang
author: Wunpawng Tam Tam (based on Hkasha Uma Awng's booklet)
subject: Society & Culture
summary: An interactive kinship tool. Choose la or num and tap a group (tinang amyu, mayu, yuji, dama, kashu kahkri) to see what to call each relative in Jinghpaw. Enter two people's parents' clans and htinggaw to check whether a marriage is allowed by custom and how they should address each other. Draft: terms come from Wunpawng Sha Ni A Shachyen Shaga Ai Lam and should be checked with elders.
keywords: shachyen, shachyen shaga, kinship, mayu, dama, kahkri, katsa, marriage, clans, htinggaw, tool

title: Kachinpedia
author: Kachinpedia team (volunteers)
subject: Apps & Learning Sites
summary: A community-supported digital archive and encyclopedia of Kachin history, culture, language and faith, with hundreds of Jinghpaw articles, a Jinghpaw–English–Burmese dictionary, the Jinghpaw Bible and hymns.
keywords: Kachinpedia, encyclopedia, articles, dictionary, Labau, Htunghking, Maumwi, Bible, hymns

title: Pawng Jinghpaw ni a bawpa mying (10) hte htinggaw mying 2337 (10 clan names and 2,337 family names of the Jinghpaw people)
author: Dureng Hkauka Zau Gam
subject: Society & Culture
summary: A Jinghpaw-language reference listing the 10 Jinghpaw clans and 2,337 htinggaw (family names). No copy found online yet.
keywords: htinggaw, clan names, amyu, family names, bawpa mying
source: Cited in Hideo Sawada (2024), "An attempt to plot the source languages of village names on a map of Kachin State, Myanmar"

title: An attempt to plot the source languages of village names on a map of Kachin State, Myanmar
author: Hideo Sawada (Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies)
subject: Language & Literature
summary: Outlines methods for determining the source languages of village names in Kachin State, using map descriptions, interviews, and family and clan names, and plots the results on a map covering Jinghpaw, Lhaovo, Lacid, Tai languages and Burmese.
keywords: village names, place names, Kachin State, map, Jinghpaw, Lhaovo, Lacid, clan names
source: John Benjamins, published in Ethnolinguistic contact across the Indo-Myanmar-Southwestern China mountains

title: PJL Archive: Kachin Oral Cultural Heritage
author: Sara Kaba Maran Pungga Ja Li and collaborators
subject: Religion
summary: Recordings of the rituals and performances of the last joiwa and dumsa (spirit priests), led by Pungga Ja Li. It includes many hours of audio and video, hundreds of photographs, and transcriptions with some translations into modern Jinghpaw and English. Its featured collection documents a 1998 funeral in Shwegu.
keywords: joiwa, dumsa, rituals, oral heritage, traditional beliefs, Pungga Ja Li, funeral

title: Excess of Love: An Oral History of the Kachin Independence Organization
author: Benjamin Williams (Williams College; advisor Prof. Eiko Maruko Siniawer)
subject: History
summary: A history of the Kachin Independence Organization based on 30 life-history interviews with 27 Kachin people in Myitkyina and Chiang Mai. It covers the KIO's founding in 1961, its schools, roads and health care in the areas it controlled after 1975, and how Kachin people remember the movement.
keywords: KIO, KIA, oral history, revolution, rebel governance, Myitkyina, Kachin identity, Rawt Malan

title: Mai Ja Yang Institute of Education (MIED)
author: KIO Education Department
subject: Schools & Education
summary: A teacher-education college in Mai Ja Yang, Kachin State, founded in 1997 by the KIO Education Department as a teacher training school and renamed in 2014. It offers a Pre-College Program, Diploma in Education, Diploma in TESOL, and Diploma in TCL, with scholarships, and the homepage lists 100 current students and 2,000 alumni.
keywords: Mai Ja Yang, teacher training, education, TESOL, diploma, KIO Education Department, Kachin State
source: Mai Ja Yang Institute of Education

title: Institute of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ILAS), Mai Ja Yang
author: Institute of Liberal Arts and Sciences
subject: Schools & Education
summary: A non-profit institute in Mai Ja Yang, Kachin State, known for its Intensive English Program (IEP). It also offers diplomas in English and in Liberal Arts, plus GED preparation. It serves IDPs, Shan students and Chinese students with limited access to education, and it marked 25 years (2001–2026) with its Ning Hpring Jubilee.
keywords: ILAS, IEP, Intensive English Program, Mai Ja Yang, liberal arts, GED, IDPs, English

title: Naushawng Development Institute (NDI)
author: Founded by Kachin scholars
subject: Schools & Education
summary: An independent, non-profit education and policy organization working for democracy, peace and community development in northern Myanmar. It runs the Naushawng Community School and Learning Center (English classes, civic engagement, scholarship help) and does research on Kachin State. "Naushawng" is the Kachin name for the leaders who guide the Manau dance, and NDI sees education as that leader. Motto: "Shape the Future, Invest in Education."
keywords: NDI, Naushawng, Manau, community school, leadership, democracy, peace building, policy research, Kachin Studies, scholarships

title: JSTOR: Research Library for Students
author: ITHAKA (non-profit)
subject: Apps & Learning Sites
summary: New to research? JSTOR is a free-to-search online library of academic articles and books. Type "Kachin" or "Jinghpaw" to find studies about our people. If an article asks you to log in, sign in through your school or college library to read it free. Use the "Cite" button to copy a ready-made citation for your paper.
keywords: JSTOR, research library, students, school papers, academic articles, citations, how to research

title: Google Scholar
author: Google
subject: Apps & Learning Sites
summary: A free search engine just for academic work: articles, theses, books and court cases. Search "Kachin" or "Jinghpaw," then click "Cite" under any result to copy a citation. Tip: set up a free Google Scholar Alert for "Kachin" to get emailed when new research comes out.
keywords: Google Scholar, research library, students, academic articles, citations, alerts, how to research

title: Internet Archive
author: Internet Archive (non-profit)
subject: Apps & Learning Sites
summary: A free online library of millions of books, documents, recordings and old websites. Many old books about the Kachin are free to read and download there, like Ola Hanson's 1896 grammar of the Kachin language.
keywords: Internet Archive, research library, students, free books, old books, downloads, how to research

title: PARADISEC
author: Pacific and Regional Archive for Digital Sources in Endangered Cultures
subject: Apps & Learning Sites
summary: A free research archive of recordings in endangered languages, including thousands of Kachin folktales and stories in Jinghpaw, many with transcriptions and English translations. Great for studying Kachin language and oral tradition.
keywords: PARADISEC, research library, students, recordings, folktales, Jinghpaw, oral tradition, how to research
